mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over a 6-month window signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 exceeding 2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses when inflation exceeds 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong consumer demand growth.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in HOUST and a fall in RSAFS above 1% month-over-month signals a shift from speculative investment to real demand, which historically precedes a stabilization in equity markets and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month and RSAFS < previous month by > 1%
regime_hint: transition from speculative to real demand
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not statistically significant at p < 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL above 0.2% month-over-month indicates a restrictive monetary policy stance with falling inflation, which historically supports higher discount rates but reduces financing costs for firms, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous month and CPIAUCSL < previous month by > 0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment rises above 7%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in PAYEMS above 0.4% month-over-month for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month by > 0.4% for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not present during periods of rising interest rates.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annual decline in CPIAUCSL below 1% for eight consecutive months signals a prolonged period of low inflation, which reduces uncertainty and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of the economic regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of financial crisis.
